Description: Rubbing is perhaps one of the oldest techniques in printmaking. Created by carefully pressing paper onto a carved or textured surface, this traditional technique is used to copy designs and texts from stone, metal or wood. Believed to be originated in East Asia and practised in China as early as nearly 2,000 years ago, rubbing was primarily used for reproducing ancient inscriptions, calligraphy and relief carvings, preserving artworks and histories. Let’s explore the cultural and historical significance behind this intriguing technique by making some rubbing art together to appreciate the beauty of Chinese artwork in this hands-on workshop!

Representing power, benevolence and good fortune, dragons are deeply rooted in the Chinese culture. In this workshop, explore how dragons continue to inspire joy through dragon dance demonstrations, crafts-making, and storytelling about the Zodiac animals.

Description: Maloya is a traditional Creole music and dance form originating from Réunion Island in the Indian Ocean. It was born out of the cultural heritage of African, Malagasy, and Indian indentured labourers brought to the island, often as an expression of resilience and a means of storytelling. The genre features rhythmic beats, call-and-response singing, and expressive dance, involving instruments such as the roulèr (bass drum), kayamb (a shaker made from sugar cane and seeds), and pikèr (bamboo). This workshop is designed to immerse participants in the cultural richness of Maloya, with activities adapted for different age groups.

Program: What It Takes to Get a Guinness World Record?
Audience: Community, Pre Primary, Schools
Available in: VIC
Genres: Storytelling
Cultural region: Multicultural
Official page: https://education.culturalinfusion.com/school-programs/what-it-takes-to-get-a-guinness-world-record/
Description: Unique to Cultural Infusion – Guinness world record holder and coach Dean presents the inside world of Guinness. It begins with GWR history in the 1950’s when Guinness Brewery Director Sir Hugh Beaver had the idea to compile a book of facts and figures to promote Guinness beer. It explores what it takes to get a Guinness world record, details Dean’s personal Guinness story of hanging out with other world record holders -including the world champion toe wrestler, sitting the world’s smallest man on his knee, and shaking the world’s biggest hand. The talk includes some action film, archival photos, live demonstrations and interactive exercises that include giving students a chance to break an unofficial world record.

In this high-energy educational workshop, participants will explore the rich history and philosophy of martial arts in Japan and have the opportunity to try various styles such as Karate, Judo, and Aikido. Translated as “the way of the warrior,” budō encompasses disciplines that require dedication, hard work, and practice. These concepts are of cultural significance and form the foundation of many Japanese martial arts. Adaptable to different ages and physical abilities, participants will gain an appreciation for the discipline, practice, and mastery that Japanese martial arts are renowned for.

Commedia dell’arte is a show that all ages can enjoy! *Adaptable to suit pre-primary and lower primary age groups*
